messages:
kevin: following up on the kernel-selection RFC 1: proposal to extract quantization profiles and kernel-targeting logic out of the hot runtime into a separate compile service. idea: produce pinned artifacts (shards of optimized kernels + metadata) per model/profile so runtime only fetches and runs. reduces runtime code-path complexity and makes artifacts reproducible. asking for pushback on safety and rollout.
leila: strong +1 for simplification. main worry: artifact explosion across model variants + sequence length dims. how do we cap artifact cardinality?
omar: cap by bucketing sequence-length classes and quantization tiers. we can evict unused artifacts after ttl and keep a metadata registry with last-access times. also need a policy for forced rebuild on model update.
sam: operationally we need fast fallback when an artifact is missing or incompatible. runtime must keep a small JIT path that can run the model unoptimized for small traffic. what's acceptable cold-start latency?
kevin: target fallback cold start <300ms for p50 warmup from local cache; for cold from network maybe 2s acceptable for batch workloads. interactive low-latency tenants need prewarm hooks.
leila: about correctness: quantization can change accuracy. we must include a verification step in the compile pipeline: run a parity pass vs baseline on a golden prompt set and compute token-diff and embedding-cosine thresholds. failing artifacts should be rejected.
anya: add regression thresholds to the manifest: max token drift, max embedding cosine delta. and record the eval vectors in the artifact metadata for audits.
kevin: rollout phases I suggest: 1) generate artifacts for a canary model and store in registry (read-only) 2) runtime can fetch artifact on demand but keep runtime-selection disabled (dry-run) 3) enable fetching for cohort A (canary tenants) with fallback routing 4) expand cohorts once metrics stable 5) deprecate runtime-selection code after 30d.
omar: what metrics? defined: infer-latency-p99, token-per-second, kernel-utilization, model-output-drift, & artifact-cache-hit-rate. also track compile-failure-rate.
sam: ownership: compile-service infra + compile-pipeline should be owned by eng-runtime, but we need clear SLOs for artifact availability (99.9) and a cost-recovery model for heavy builds. platform shouldn't silently absorb.
leila: build provenance: artifacts must include compiler version, toolchain checksum, model commit and quantization params. we need an immutable artifact id.
kevin: rollback: keep a compatibility manifest mapping model-version -> runtime-default-behavior. if artifact verification fails after cutover, flip manifest to prefer runtime JIT. need an emergency kill switch.
anya: observability: traces should include artifact-id and compile-hash and the fallback-reason. add a dashboard with per-artifact regressions and a list of tenants using an artifact.
kevin: ops checklist draft: ```- implement artifact manifest schema (json)
- add compile job to CI with parity checks
- artifact registry service + retention policy (30d default)
- runtime client: fetch + verify artifact signature + cache
- implement dry-run mode (compare outputs, no routing)
- enable canary cohort A (5 tenants) with fallback gating
- ramp cohorts B,C -> global
- post-cutover: deprecate runtime path after 30d and run code prune
- add cost-allocation tag on compile jobs
```
omar: one implementation concern: where do we store large kernel blobs? object store with signed URLs, but registry should keep metadata and integrity checksums. signed URLs & short TTLs reduce risk.
sam: security: artifact signing via KMS and signature verification at runtime mandatory. also scan compile env for secrets to avoid embedding.
leila: performance experiment: simulate artifact cache-miss storm and measure downstream latency and egress. need throttles or staged prewarm.
kevin: agree. plan to add prewarm hooks: admin API to pin artifacts to zones and a reactive prefetch on model-publish.
infra-bot: compile-service pipeline: "kernel-compiler-v1" wired into staging at 2025-07-03T21:10Z. parity job added to CI.
anya: final ask: add an evaluation notebook that reproduces parity runs so data-science can validate metrics.
kevin: will attach notebook and update RFC with the manifest proto, rollout gates, and ownership. react with :thumbsup: if you approve the phased plan and owners.
sam: :thumbsup:
leila: :thumbsup:
omar: :thumbsup:
anya: :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks all  I'll create the epic and tag runtime + infra teams. leave comments here if you want more gates.
